subject: Error in histogram of a gdistsamp object

messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: Error in histogram of a gdistsamp object
parts:
Dear list members,

I am trying to do an histogram on a gdistsamp object but I got an error (see below):

> m1 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", output="density")
> summary(m1)

Call:
gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~1, phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1, 
    data = umf, output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq")

Abundance (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE    z P(>|z|)
     3.14 0.333 9.45 3.4e-21

Availability (logit-scale):
 Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
    -0.33 0.538 -0.614   0.539

Detection (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     2.41 0.129 18.7 1.12e-77

AIC: 224.8965 
Number of sites: 5
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 42 
Bootstrap iterations: 0 

> hist(m1, xlab="Distance (m)", ylab="Probability density", main="", ylim=c(0, 0.1), cex.lab=0.7, cex.axis=0.7, las=1)
Error en hist.default(m1, xlab = "Distance (m)", ylab = "Probability density",  : 
  'x' must be numeric

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error in histogram of a gdistsamp object
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Hopefully someone will correct me if I'm wrong, but I think the standard approach is to assume closure, and then to regard the number of visits as "effort". You could do this using distsamp() by supplying the number of visits as an offset, eg

distsamp(~1 ~offset(log(nVisits)), umf, output="abund")

Note that you will need to sum the counts for each distance interval over the number of visits, ie if there were 4 distance intervals and 5 visits, your "y" matrix needs 4 columns, not 20 as would be required by gdistsamp.

Richard
